title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
This is a synthetic image presented as a documentary photograph of real people. The alteration happened in the production of promotional material, after the original Lunar New Year photo existed and before it was printed on campus banners. A real student was removed and replaced with a fabricated person, and other students were reshaped, with no indication to viewers that the image had been generated or edited. The university has said the alteration and the absence of disclosure both violated its own policy, which prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements.

Catching it required only a comparison at the point of approval, between the file going to the printer and the original photograph, and a check against the policy that governed the material. The university's statement that it is now working to ensure proper review of all materials indicates that this check was not applied when the banners were made. Training and review are the controls that were missing, not technical detection.

What is not established is who performed the alteration, whether the substitution of a Black woman for a Hispanic student was deliberate, and whether anyone faced consequences. The university's acknowledgement covers the fact of the alteration and the policy violation, not intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior at Stanford majoring in human biology, appeared in a 2024 Lunar New Year photo with two other students. The university's dining service posted the image online. When Stanford later used the photo on campus banners last week, Ramirez had been replaced by an image of a Black woman, and the other students were altered to look thinner. Ramirez learned about the change from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its AI policy strictly prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said both the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide more training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
